knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=The input data containing transcript-level expression values (can be a matrix, data.frame, tximport list, DGEList, or SummarizedExperiment) ;; genes=A vector of gene names mapping each transcript row to its corresponding gene for aggregation ;; method=The diversity measure to calculate ("laplace", "gini", "shannon", "simpson", etc.) in calculate_diversity, or the aggregation method ("mean" or "median") in calculate_difference ;; norm=Logical value; if TRUE, normalizes entropy values to the number of transcripts per gene ;; tpm=Logical value; set to TRUE to extract TPM values from a tximport list (default is FALSE, which extracts raw read counts) ;; assayno=An optional numeric value specifying which assay to analyze when using a SummarizedExperiment input ;; samples=A vector or column name in colData specifying the sample categories/conditions ;; control=The name of the control condition in the samples vector ;; test=The statistical test to use for differential analysis ("wilcoxon" or "label shuffling") ;; randomizations=The number of random shuffles to perform if using the label shuffling test (default is 100) ;; pcorr=The p-value correction method to use (default is "BH" for Benjamini & Hochberg)
- alternatives: The documentation mentions that transcript-level expression estimates should be generated using upstream tools such as STAR alignment followed by featureCounts, RSEM, Salmon, or Kallisto, and imported using tximport.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have transcript-level expression data across multiple samples and conditions and want to analyze changes in alternative splicing diversity at the gene level rather than individual transcript usage.
- pitfalls: Using raw read counts that are not normalized for transcript length will bias diversity calculations toward longer transcripts; length-normalized values like TPM are highly recommended. Genes with only a single isoform are automatically excluded because diversity cannot be calculated. Samples with zero expression across all isoforms of a gene will result in NA diversity values. For statistical testing, the Wilcoxon test requires at least 3 samples per category (minimum 8 total), and the label shuffling test requires at least 5 samples per category.

workflows.name: splicing_diversity_and_differential_analysis
workflows.intent: Calculate transcript isoform diversity (Laplace entropy and Gini index) from transcript expression data and identify genes with significant diversity changes between conditions.
input: transcript_expression.tsv (matrix or data frame of transcript-level expression values where rows are transcripts and columns are samples)
gene_vector.tsv (a vector mapping each transcript row to its corresponding gene)
sample_metadata.tsv (a vector or table of sample conditions/groups)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter out low-expression transcripts to reduce variability ;; 2. Calculate gene-level splicing diversity using calculate_diversity() ;; 3. Append sample condition metadata to the resulting SummarizedExperiment object ;; 4. Perform differential diversity analysis between conditions using calculate_difference()
workflows.code:
library("SplicingFactory")
library("SummarizedExperiment")

# Load dataset
data(tcga_brca_luma_dataset)

# Extract gene names
genes <- tcga_brca_luma_dataset[, 1]

# Extract read count data without gene names
readcounts <- tcga_brca_luma_dataset[, -1]

# Data filtering and preprocessing
tokeep <- rowSums(readcounts > 5) > 5
readcounts <- readcounts[tokeep, ]
genes      <- genes[tokeep]

# Transcript diversity calculation
laplace_entropy <- calculate_diversity(readcounts, genes,  method = "laplace",
                                       norm = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

gini_index <- calculate_diversity(readcounts, genes, method = "gini",
                                  verbose = TRUE)

# Update the SummarizedExperiment object with a new sample metadata column for sample types
colData(laplace_entropy) <- cbind(colData(laplace_entropy),
                                      sample_type = ifelse(grepl("_N", laplace_entropy$samples),
                                                           "Normal", "Tumor"))

# Calculate significant entropy changes
entropy_significance <- calculate_difference(x = laplace_entropy, samples = "sample_type",
                                             control = "Normal",
                                             method = "mean", test = "wilcoxon",
                                             verbose = TRUE)
